questions.question: A service handles 100 million generations in a 30-day month. What is the approximate average generation rate before peak headroom?
options: 4 images per second
39 images per second
386 images per second
3,860 images per second
questions.explanation: A 30-day month has 2,592,000 seconds. Dividing 100 million by that duration gives about 38.6 images per second.

questions.question: Which measurement is required to size the accelerator fleet defensibly?
options: Concurrent users divided by GPU memory
Prompt tokens per month without image settings
Images per accelerator at the target resolution, steps, batch policy, and p95
The model's parameter count alone
questions.explanation: Fleet sizing needs a production-shaped throughput benchmark. Resolution, denoising steps, precision, batching, and the latency target all change images per accelerator.

questions.question: Why does the design inspect both the prompt and the generated image?
options: The output gate replaces the need for prompt admission and quotas
Prompt filtering saves unsafe compute, while output inspection catches harmful pixels produced from prompts that passed
Two classifiers guarantee there can be no false positives
The prompt classifier is used only to choose image resolution
questions.explanation: The two gates cover different failure points. Prompt checks reject clear violations early, while output checks evaluate what the stochastic model actually created.

questions.question: The prompt and output classifiers pass, but generation provenance could not be written. What should the release state machine do?
options: Release the image and reconstruct provenance later
Delete the job and charge the user again
Hold the output because provenance is part of the release invariant
Skip every safety check on the retry
questions.explanation: The lesson defines provenance as a mandatory release condition. A passing safety score does not permit an untraceable image to leave the system.

questions.question: Which overload response preserves the design's invariants?
options: Disable output moderation until the queue drains
Retry every timed-out generation without an attempt limit
Offer a lower-resolution preview or a longer ETA while retaining every release gate
Publish directly from GPU workers to reduce storage latency
questions.explanation: Quality, admission, and waiting time may degrade explicitly. Prompt policy, output policy, identity checks, and provenance remain mandatory.

questions.question: Why should unit economics track cost per released image instead of only cost per generation attempt?
options: Released-image cost includes retries, cancellations, quarantines, and failed attempts that consume compute without producing user value
Generation attempts never consume accelerator capacity
Released images do not use storage or CDN bandwidth
The metric removes the need to measure queue latency
questions.explanation: Cost per released image connects infrastructure spending to a successful product outcome and exposes waste from retries, rejected outputs, and abandoned work.
